Rashi on Eruvin 92a:10:1.english: Just as a courtyard, whose partitions are conspicuous - For behold, it has partitions.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:10:2.hebrew: אף גג - נהי נמי דשרינן ליה במחיצות תחתונות משום גוד אסיק, מיהו מחיצות ניכרות בעינן — שלא יהא גג בולט חוצה להם; דאי לא מינכרא, לא אמרינן גוד אסיק, וגדול נמי אסור, דאין לו שום מחיצה, וכל שאין לו מחיצות אינו רשות היחיד. כל גגין שלהן חלקין היו, ולא משופעין:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:10:2.english: So too, a roof - Even though we permit it [to carry on a roof] by means of the lower partitions due to [the principle of] gud asik [extend and raise the walls upward], nevertheless, we require conspicuous partitions — that the roof should not protrude beyond them; for if [the wall] is not conspicuous, we do not say gud asik, and the large [roof] too would be prohibited, as it has no partition at all, and anything that has no partitions is not a private domain. All of their roofs were flat and not sloped.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:11:1.hebrew: ולשמואל - דאמר: אפילו לא מינכרא אמרינן גוד אסיק — להכי תננהי גבי הדדי: דמה חצר דדרסי לה רבים, אף גג, האי דקתני קטן אסור — משום דדרסי רבים מזה לזה, דהוי לה מחיצה תחתונה שביניהם מחיצה נדרסת, ולא מצית למיגד ואסוקה. אבל אי לא דרסי בהן, אף קטן שרי, דאמרינן גוד אסיק ותפסיק המחיצה ביניהם, ואע"ג דמכסיא ולא מינכרא:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:11:1.english: And according to Shmuel - Who said that even if [the partition] is not noticeable, we say "extend and raise" — that is why [the Mishnah] taught them alongside each other: For just as a courtyard is [a place] where many tread, so too [on] a roof, that which it taught, "[the] small [one] is forbidden," is because many tread from this one to that one, so that the lower partition between them becomes a trodden partition, and you cannot extend and raise it. But if [people] do not tread on them, even [the] small [one] is permitted, for we say "extend and raise," and the partition will divide between them, even though it is covered and not noticeable.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:12:1.english: The residents of the large [courtyard] rule over the small [one] - And draw it to themselves.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:12:2.english: And the residents of the small [courtyard] do not - Rule over the large [courtyard] to draw them to themselves.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:13:1.hebrew: אסור לזרוע את הקטנה - דכמאן דהויא קטנה כולה בתוך גדולה דמי. ואפילו מרחיק ארבע אמות מן הגפנים — שאפילו בתוך הגדולה מותר להרחיק ולזרוע — הכא אסור, דקתני מתני': "מפני שהיא כפתחה של גדולה", אלמא כולה כחד פתח משוה לה:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:13:1.english: It is prohibited to sow the small [courtyard] - For it is considered as though the small [courtyard] is entirely within the large [one]. And even if one distances [the seeds] four cubits from the vines — whereas even inside the large [courtyard itself] it is permitted to distance [by four cubits] and sow — here it is prohibited, as the Mishnah teaches: “Because it is like the opening of the large [courtyard],” which shows that [the Mishnah] equates all of it to a single opening.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:1:1.hebrew: ומי אמר ר' יוחנן הכי - הלכה כר' שמעון, ואפילו עירבו, דחצירות רשות אחת:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:1:1.english: And did Rabbi Yoḥanan say this - [That the] halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, and even [if] they established an eiruv, that courtyards are a single domain?

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:1:2.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יורידו למטה - אלמא, אסור להוציא מחצר לחבירתה. אי אמרת בשלמא בעירבו אסור — אוקימנא להא בעירבו; אבל השתא, במאי תוקמא:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:1:2.english: Provided that they do not take [it] down below - Evidently, it is forbidden to carry from [one] courtyard to another. Granted if you say [that] when they established an eiruv it is forbidden, we could establish this [mishnah as referring to a case where] they established an eiruv; but now, in what [case] can you establish it?

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:2:1.hebrew: שלא יהא זה עומד במקומו - בקרקעית החצר. ל"א: "שיהא זה עומד במקומו" גרסינן, ועל ראש הכותל קאמר:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:2:1.english: That this one should not stand in his place - [That is,] on the ground of the courtyard. Another version: We read, “That this one should stand in his place,” and it is referring to the top of the wall.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:3:1.english: And if Rabbi did not teach it - [Meaning,] this teaching in his Mishnah.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:3:2.hebrew: רבי חייא - שסידר וסתם את הברייתא, ותלמידו היה:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:3:2.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya - Who arranged and redacted the Baraita, and he was his student.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:3:3.hebrew: מניין לו - זה הפירוש. ולעולם "למטה" דסתם רבי מתני' — בבתים קאמר, שלא יוריד מראש הכותל ויוליך לביתו:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:3:3.english: From where does he [know] it - [From where does he know] this interpretation? And indeed, [by the word] “down below” that Rabbi taught anonymously in the Mishnah, he meant regarding houses — that one may not take [the fruit] down from atop the wall and carry [it] to his house.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:4:1.hebrew: וחורבה אחת ביניהם - לא שנא שלהם ולא שנא של אחרים — דהא אוקמא כר"ש, שאין חילוק רשות אלא בבתים. וכגון שאינה פרוצה לרשות הרבים:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:4:1.english: And one ruin between them - [It] makes no difference whether [it belongs to] them or whether [it belongs to] others, for this [case] is established in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, [who holds] that there is no division of domain except with regard to houses. And [this is a case] where [the ruin] is not breached to the public domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:4:2.hebrew: אחת עירבה - לעצמה, ושכיחי מאני דבתים בגווה:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:4:2.english: One established an eiruv - For itself, and vessels from the houses are commonly found within it.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:5:1.hebrew: אמר רב הונא נותנין החורבה לזו שלא עירבה - להוציא לה כלים ששבתו בחצר, דהא לא שכיחי בה מאני דבתים, הואיל ולא עירבה. אבל לשעירבה — לא, דרב הונא תלמידו דרב הוה, דאמר: הלכה כר"ש בשלא עירבו, אבל עירבו — לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:5:1.english: Rav Huna said: They assign the ruin to this [courtyard] that did not establish an eiruv - To take out into it vessels that rested in the courtyard, as household vessels are not commonly found in it, since it did not establish an eiruv. But to the [courtyard] that established an eiruv, no — for Rav Huna was the disciple of Rav, who said: The halakhah is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon when they did not establish an eiruv, but when they established an eiruv, no.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:5:2.hebrew: וחייא בר רב אמר אף לשעירבה - אני שמעתי מאבא: "אף לשעירבה נותנין אותה", ומדעתי אני מפרש דהאי דאמר אבא "אף לשעירבה" — לאסור את שתיהן קאמר; דגזר לא עירבה אטו עירבה, דאי מפקי הני לגווה — הני נמי אתו ומפקי:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:5:2.english: And Ḥiyya bar Rav said: Even to [the courtyard] that established an eiruv - [Ḥiyya bar Rav was saying:] I heard from Father [Rav]: "Even to [the courtyard] that established an eiruv we assign it"; and of my own reasoning I explain that this which Father said, "Even to [the courtyard] that established an eiruv," he said [it] to prohibit both of them, for he decreed [against the courtyard that] did not establish an eiruv on account of [the one that] established an eiruv; for if these [residents] carry out into it, those [residents] will also come and carry out.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:5:3.hebrew: וא"ת - במה ששמעתי "אף לשעירבה", להתיר קאמר אבא, דשתיהן מותרות, ולא גזר אבא בעירבה משום מאני דבתים — קשיא לי במילתא דאבא, דאמר לעיל: "הלכה כר"ש, והוא שלא עירבו, אבל עירבו לא": מפני מה אין נותנים חצר שלא עירבה לחצר שעירבה? תכניס כליה לתוך חבירתה ותוציאם, הא לא גזר רב בחורבה?! כלומר, נהי נמי דתשני לי דהא דאמר רב לעיל "אבל עירבה לא", מודה הוא דאותה שלא עירבה מכנסת ומוציאה כליה לתוך שעירבה, דהא לא שכיחי בה בשלא עירבה מאני דבתים, ואע"ג דבהא שכיחי לא חיישינן, דסתמא כי משתמש איניש במאני דידיה משתמש ולא בחבריה — מיהו קשיא לי: אמאי אסר אבא כשעירבה להכניס לשלא עירבה? הא לא גזר לגבי חורבה:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:5:3.english: And if you say - [If you were to say that] in what I heard, "even to one that made an eiruv," Abba meant to permit, [so] that both are permitted, and Abba did not decree in [the case of a courtyard that] made an eiruv on account of household articles — I have a difficulty with Abba's statement, for he said above: "The halakhah is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, provided that they did not make an eiruv; but if they made an eiruv, no." Why do we not assign the courtyard that did not make an eiruv to the courtyard that made an eiruv? Let it bring its articles into its fellow [courtyard] and take them out! After all, Rav did not decree [a prohibition] in the case of a ruin! That is to say: Even granted that you could answer me that regarding that which Rav said above, "but if it made an eiruv, no," he concedes that that [courtyard] which did not make an eiruv may bring in and take out its articles into the one that made an eiruv, since in the one that did not make an eiruv household articles are not commonly found [in the courtyard], and even though in this one they are commonly found, we are not concerned, for ordinarily when a person uses articles, he uses his own articles and not his fellow's — nevertheless, I have a difficulty: Why did Abba forbid [the courtyard], when it made an eiruv, to bring [articles] into the one that did not make an eiruv? After all, he did not decree with respect to a ruin!

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:6:1.hebrew: התם כיון דמינטר - כלומר, אף לשעירבה דקאמר רב — להיתר קאמר. וגבי חצירות, אמאי גזר? משום דכיון דמינטרי כלים בחצר, שכיחי לאפוקי מאני טובא, וחיישינן דלמא מחלפי מאני דבתים במאני דחצר ומפקי לחבירתה, שהרי נשמרים גם בתוכה. אבל חורבה — לא עבידי בה אינשי לאפוקי מאני טובא:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:6:1.english: There, since [they] are protected - That is to say, that which Rav said, "Even to the one that made an eiruv," he said to permit [both courtyards]. And regarding courtyards, why did he decree [a prohibition]? Because since vessels are protected in a courtyard, it is common to bring out many vessels, and we are concerned lest vessels of the houses be confused with vessels of the courtyard and they will take [them] out into the neighboring [courtyard], for behold, they are protected within it as well. But [in] a ruin, people are not accustomed to bring out many vessels into it.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:7:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי חייא בר רב אמר אף לשעירבה ושתיהן מותרות ואם תאמר שתיהן אסורות - וטעמא: משום דשמעינן ליה לאבא דקאמר "אבל עירבו לא". אלמא על כרחך, אפילו דחקת למילתיה דאבא לאוקומא להאי דאסר — בשעירבה הוא דאסר לטלטל כליה לשלא עירבה, אבל שלא עירבה מותרת לתוך שעירבה — שמעינן מיהא דאין נותנין שלא עירבה לשעירבה. אלמא גזר בעירבה משום מאני דבתים, ובחורבה נמי על כרחך שעירבה אסורה בה, וכי אמר אבא "דיהבי לה לתרוייהו" — לאיסורא קאמר! — לא דמי:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:7:1.english: Some say Ḥiyya bar Rav said: Even to the one that established an eiruv, and both are permitted. And if you say both are prohibited - And the reason [one would say that both are prohibited is] because we heard Abba [Rav] saying: “However, [if] they established an eiruv, no.” Thus perforce, even if you press Abba’s statement to establish that [regarding] this [case] which he prohibited, it was [only] for the one that established an eiruv that he prohibited moving its vessels into the one that did not establish an eiruv, but the one that did not establish an eiruv is permitted [to move its vessels] into the one that established an eiruv — nevertheless, we deduce that they do not confer [the rights of] the one that did not establish an eiruv to the one that established an eiruv. Evidently, he decreed regarding the one that established an eiruv on account of vessels from the houses, and in [the case of] a ruin as well, perforce the one that established an eiruv should be prohibited in it, and when Abba said that they give it to both of them, he said [so] to prohibit [them both]! — [The Gemara answers:] They are not comparable:

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:7:2.hebrew: התם - גבי חצירות, כיון דמינטרי מאני בחצר חבירו כבחצירו, עבידי לאפוקי לה מאני טובא, וחיישינן דלא ליפוק לה מאני דבתים; אבל חורבה — לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:7:2.english: There - With regard to courtyards: Since vessels are protected in one's fellow's courtyard just as in his [own] courtyard, people are prone to bring out many vessels to it, and we are concerned lest one bring out to it vessels of the houses; but [in] a ruin, [they are] not [protected].

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:8:1.hebrew: הגדול מותר - להכניס לו כלי הבית שלמטה, ואין בני הקטן אוסרין עליו, דלגבי גדול הך פרצה פתח הוא, דשרי בגיפופי, וכגון דאין הפרצה יותר מעשר. אבל קטן — אסור לו להוציא כלי הבית, דבני גדול אסרי עליה, דנפרץ לו במלואו. ודברי הכל היא, דאפילו ר' מאיר לא אמר "גגין רשות אחת" אלא לכלים ששבתו בתוכן, אבל לכלים ששבתו בבתים — לא, דומיא דחצר קטנה שנפרצה לגדולה, דלכולי עלמא חצירות רשות אחת הן, ולענין כלי הבתים אסרה גדולה אקטנה:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:8:1.english: The large [roof] is permitted - to bring into it vessels from the house below, and the residents of the small [roof] do not prohibit [carrying] upon it, for with respect to the large [roof], this breach is [considered] an entrance, which is permitted by [virtue of its] jambs, and [this is] where the breach is not more than ten [cubits]. However, [regarding] the small [roof], it is prohibited for [its resident] to bring out vessels of the house, for the residents of the large [roof] prohibit [carrying] upon it, because it is breached toward it in its full width. And this is agreed upon by all, for even Rabbi Meir said [that] roofs are a single domain only regarding vessels that rested within them [at the onset of Shabbat], but regarding vessels that rested in houses, [he did] not — similar to a small courtyard that was breached into a large one, for according to everyone, courtyards are a single domain, and [yet] with regard to vessels of the houses, the large [courtyard] renders [carrying] prohibited for the small one.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:8:2.hebrew: גדולה מותרת - להוציא כלי הבתים שבה, אם עירבה לעצמה, ולא אסרי עלה בני קטנה:
Rashi on Eruvin 92a:8:2.english: The large [courtyard] is permitted - to bring out the utensils of the houses that are in it, if it made an eruv for itself, and the residents of the small [courtyard] do not prohibit [carrying] upon it.

Rashi on Eruvin 92a:9:1.english: Two - A courtyard and a roof.

Tosafot on Eruvin 92a:11:1.english: "So too, the roof is a place where multitudes tread" - This is in accordance with the first version of Rav Yosef above.

Tosafot on Eruvin 92a:13:1.hebrew: גפנים בגדולה אסור לזרוע את הקטנה - למ"ד (לעיל עירובין דף ט:) נראה מבחוץ ושוה מבפנים נידון משום לחי ופתח — מיירי בנכנסין כותלי קטנה לגדולה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 92a:13:1.english: "[If there are] vines in the large [courtyard], it is prohibited to sow the small one" - According to the one who holds (above, Eruvin 9b) [that that which is] visible from the outside and even from the inside is judged as a side post and an entrance, [the Mishnah] is dealing with [a case where] the walls of the small [courtyard] enter into the large one.

Tosafot on Eruvin 92a:1:1.hebrew: והא אמר רבי יוחנן הלכה כסתם משנה - וקשה, דסתם ואח"כ מחלוקת הוא, ואמר בהחולץ (יבמות דף מב:) דאין הלכה כסתם! ואע"ג דלכל הפחות חשיב סתם כרבים כלפי היחיד, הכא אין נפקא מינה, דבלאו הכי פליגי רבנן עליה. ותירץ הרר"א כהן, דעיקר קושיא לר"י אינה אלא דלא גזר, ובזה הדבר הוי מחלוקת ואח"כ סתם: מחלוקת בשלש חצירות במי שהוציאוהו (לעיל עירובין דף מה:), וסתם בפרק חלון (לעיל עירובין דף עו:); אבל הכא, לא פליגי בגזירה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 92a:1:1.english: "But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say that the halakha is in accordance with an unattributed mishna?" - And this is difficult, for it is an unattributed [mishna] and afterwards a dispute, and [Rabbi Yoḥanan] said in [the chapter entitled] Hacholetz (Yevamot 42b) that the halakha is not in accordance with an unattributed [mishna in such a case]! And even though at the very least an unattributed [mishna] is considered like [the opinion of] the majority against an individual, here there is no practical difference, for even without that [unattributed mishna], the Rabbis disagree with him [Rabbi Shimon]. And Harav R. A. Cohen answered that the main difficulty against Rabbi Yoḥanan is only that [Rabbi Shimon] did not decree [a rabbinic safeguard], and regarding this matter it is a dispute and afterwards an unattributed [mishna]: the dispute is [regarding] three courtyards in [the chapter entitled] Mi SheHotzi'uhu (above, Eruvin 45b), and the unattributed [mishna] is in the chapter [entitled] Chelon (above, Eruvin 76b); but here, they do not disagree about a decree.

Tosafot on Eruvin 92a:5:1.hebrew: מפני מה אין נותנין חצר שלא עירבה לחצר שעירבה - משום דאיירי באחת עירבה ואחת לא עירבה, נקט האי לישנא; והוא הדין דהוה מצי למימר: מפני מה אין נותנין חצר שעירבה לשעירבה? ובקונטרס פירש שפיר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 92a:5:1.english: "For what reason did they not confer a courtyard that did not establish an eiruv to a courtyard that established an eiruv?" - Because [the Gemara] is dealing with [a case where] one [courtyard] established an eiruv and one did not establish an eiruv, it used this phrasing; and the same applies, for it could have said: "For what reason did they not confer a courtyard that established an eiruv to [a courtyard] that established an eiruv?" And in the Kunteres [Rashi], it is explained well.

Tosafot on Eruvin 92a:7:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי אף לשעירבה ושתיהם מותרות - לפי האיכא דאמרי, קשיא הא דאמר בפרק הדר (לעיל עירובין דף עד.): ר' יוחנן אמר אף לחורבה, ורבי יוחנן לטעמיה — דלא גזר דילמא אתי לאפוקי מאני דבתים לחצר, והכא נמי לא גזר דילמא אתי לאפוקי מאני דבתים לחורבה. ומאי "לטעמיה" הוא? דהא אפילו רב דגזר, הכא גבי חורבה לא גזר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 92a:7:1.english: "Some say: Even to [the courtyard] that established an eiruv, and both are permitted" - According to the "Some say" [version], that which [the Gemara] said in the chapter [entitled] Hadar (above, Eruvin 74a) is difficult: "Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even to a ruin"; and "Rabbi Yoḥanan followed his reasoning, for he does not decree lest one come to take out house vessels into the courtyard, and here too he does not decree lest one come to take out house vessels into the ruin" — and why is it [described as] "following his reasoning"? For even Rav, who decrees [regarding courtyards], here regarding a ruin did not decree.
